title: QUIC RFC 9368 Version Information Parse-Failure Close Architecture
purpose: Describe how malformed peer Version Information is promoted from transport-parameter parser failure into a local TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR close.
design_summary: The transport-parameter codec remains the canonical parser for Version Information values. When the TLS transcript parser encounters a quic_transport_parameters extension whose Version Information tuple fails codec validation, it marks the fatal transcript step with an internal transport-parameter parse-failure alert marker instead of the generic transcript parse-failure marker. The transport-facing TLS bridge maps that marker to QUIC TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR, and the connection runtime consumes the fatal TLS update through the normal local-close path so malformed peer Version Information closes the connection.
risks: If malformed transport parameters are collapsed back into generic TLS parse failures, RFC 9368 parse-failure closes can regress to PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
If tests only assert codec rejection, they do not prove endpoint close behavior.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This slice covers malformed Version Information in peer transport parameters during the handshake. It does not change compatible-version selection or Retry and 0-RTT behavior.
